nodes.title: the Nyrduth signature
nodes.statement: The Nyrduth system concerns objects called glimyuks. There are exactly 6 of them: fexvash, kamorn, muxreld, quilisk, ovifal, kanyr. Two operations are written & and :. One relation is written >-, read as "precedes".

nodes.title: the Nyrduth combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x & y for every pair of glimyuks is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for :. The pairs standing in the >- relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all glimyuks x and y, x & y is again a glimyuk.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all glimyuks x, y, z: (x & y) & z = x & (y & z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all glimyuks x and y: x & y = y & x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a glimyuk fexvash with fexvash & x = x & fexvash = x for every x.

nodes.title: an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a glimyuk kanyr with kanyr & x = x & kanyr = kanyr for every x.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all glimyuks x and y, x : y is again a glimyuk.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all glimyuks x, y, z: (x : y) : z = x : (y : z).

nodes.title: commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all glimyuks x and y: x : y = y : x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is a glimyuk kanyr with kanyr : x = x for every x.

nodes.title: self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: For every glimyuk x: x : x = x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every glimyuk x: x >- x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all glimyuks x and y: if x >- y and y >- x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all glimyuks x, y, z: if x >- y and y >- z then x >- z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all glimyuks x and y, at least one of x >- y and y >- x holds.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: For all glimyuks x, y, z: if x >- y then (z & x) >- (z & y) and (x & z) >- (y & z).

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the second operation
nodes.statement: For all glimyuks x, y, z: if x >- y then (z : x) >- (z : y) and (x : z) >- (y : z).

nodes.title: the system does not have reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: Some glimyuk x admits no glimyuk y for which x & y and y & x both land on a neutral object.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kamorn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every glimyuk x: x & x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kamorn, value = muxreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all glimyuks x, y, z: if x & y = x & z then y = z.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kamorn, y = ovifal, z = kanyr, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have spreading of the second operation over the first
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all glimyuks x, y, z: x : (y & z) = (x : y) & (x : z), and the same on the right.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kamorn, y = kamorn, z = kamorn, left = kamorn, right = muxreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have the absorption pair
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all glimyuks x and y: x & (x : y) = x and x : (x & y) = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kamorn, y = kamorn, value = muxreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: sibtez glimyuks
nodes.statement: A glimyuk x is called sibtez when x & x = x.

nodes.title: glimyuks that shenovi
nodes.statement: Two glimyuks x and y are said to shenovi when x & y = y & x.

nodes.title: tuopal collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of glimyuks is tuopal when x & y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the mornclo of a glimyuk
nodes.statement: The mornclo of a glimyuk x is the collection of glimyuks y for which x >- y holds.

nodes.title: the muxclo
nodes.statement: The glimyuk fexvash is called the muxclo of the system. It is the unique glimyuk that leaves every glimyuk unchanged under &.

nodes.title: the fexsol
nodes.statement: The fexsol of the system is the collection of glimyuks that shenovi with every glimyuk.

nodes.title: the hobkorr
nodes.statement: The hobkorr is the collection of all sibtez glimyuks.

nodes.title: the xilvor of a glimyuk
nodes.statement: The xilvor of a glimyuk x, written [x], is the smallest tuopal collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a mornisk
nodes.statement: A glimyuk f is a mornisk when f >- y holds for every glimyuk y, that is, when the mornclo of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: glimshen glimyuks
nodes.statement: A glimyuk x is glimshen when x & x equals the muxclo.

nodes.title: the migel of a glimyuk
nodes.statement: The migel of a glimyuk x is the number of glimyuks in its xilvor [x].

nodes.title: the nyrvex
nodes.statement: The nyrvex of the system is the collection of glimyuks whose migel is largest.

nodes.title: keldthra pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct glimyuks x and y form a keldthra pair when x >- y and y >- x both hold, that is, when each lies in the mornclo of the other.

nodes.title: the muxclo is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one glimyuk e with e & x = x & e = x for every glimyuk x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every glimyuk unchanged.
Then e & f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e & f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the muxclo lies in the fexsol
nodes.statement: The muxclo shenovis with every glimyuk.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the muxclo and x any glimyuk.
Then e & x = x and x & e = x.
So e & x = x & e, which is what it means to shenovi.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the fexsol.

nodes.title: the fexsol is tuopal
nodes.statement: If x and y both shenovi with every glimyuk, then so does x & y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the fexsol and let z be any glimyuk.
Then (x & y) & z = x & (y & z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each shenovis with everything.
So x & y shenovis with z, and the fexsol is tuopal.

nodes.title: the xilvor of a glimyuk is tuopal
nodes.statement: For every glimyuk x, the collection [x] is tuopal.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under &.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the xilvor is contained in every tuopal collection
nodes.statement: If S is tuopal and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a glimyuk is sibtez exactly when its migel is one
nodes.statement: x & x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x & x = x then {x} is already closed under &.
So [x] = {x} and the migel is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x & x, which is then x.

nodes.title: where the migel divides the number of glimyuks breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every glimyuk x, the migel of x divides 6.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kamorn, reach = 5, size = 6, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the xilvor of a fexsol glimyuk stays in the fexsol
nodes.statement: If x lies in the fexsol then every glimyuk of [x] lies in the fexsol.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The fexsol is tuopal.
[x] is the smallest tuopal collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the fexsol is one.

nodes.title: the hobkorr is tuopal
nodes.statement: If x and y are both sibtez then so is x & y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be sibtez.
The claim asks whether (x & y) & (x & y) returns x & y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: mornclos are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the mornclo of x, then the mornclo of y is contained in the mornclo of x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x >- y and let z satisfy y >- z.
Transitivity gives x >- z.
So every member of the mornclo of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one mornisk
nodes.statement: No two distinct glimyuks can both be mornisks.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f >- h, since h is any object, and h >- f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the system has a mornisk
nodes.statement: Some glimyuk mornisks the whole system.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: the relation survives combination on the right
nodes.statement: If x >- y then (x & z) >- (y & z) for every glimyuk z.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y lie in the mornclo of x.
Compatibility applies the operation to both sides at once.
Nothing else is needed, since z was arbitrary.

nodes.title: no keldthra pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct glimyuks lie in each other's mornclo.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.

nodes.title: every glimyuk lies in the fexsol
nodes.statement: Every pair of glimyuks shenovis.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The fexsol is defined by shenoviing with everything.
The claim is that x & y = y & x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: where every glimyuk is sibtez breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: x & x = x for every glimyuk x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = kamorn, value = muxreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where some glimyuk reaches every other breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: There is a glimyuk whose xilvor is the whole system.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case largest_span = 5, size = 6, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the relation reads the same in both directions breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: If x >- y then y >- x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = fexvash, y = kamorn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the muxclo swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e & x equals the muxclo for every glimyuk x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case anchor = fexvash, x = kamorn, value = kamorn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the second operation keeps the fexsol intact
nodes.statement: If x and y lie in the fexsol then so does x : y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The fexsol is already tuopal under &.
The second operation is defined on every pair.
The claim is that : respects the fexsol as well.
